content.thinking:
Interesting subtlety here: the flag revert didn't actually work — logs at 07:17-07:19 still show monthly-spend-feature=on even after the revert attempt at 07:16:19. So the real root cause is the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47 triggered by the flag ramp, compounded by the revert failing to stick.

I should be careful writing this up: I need to flag the second candidate's claim about toggling reproducing the issue as speculative, not confirmed. The root cause should be stated with appropriate uncertainty — flag ramp between 07:09-07:11 exposed a latent divide-by-zero on the account page, strongly supported by logs but not fully confirmed since the fix attempt failed and the flag kept showing "on."

For the executive summary I want to note this affected the account page on the online shop, roughly a third of requests failing starting 07:10 UTC and still ongoing at least 11 minutes when metrics ended, with an automated fix that didn't work and escalation to humans — avoiding specific component names where possible, and I should list my assumptions clearly.

assumptions: Impact is bounded, not measured: the service had not recovered by the last minute of metrics read, so the ~11 minute duration and every impact figure derived from it are lower bounds.

That the flag ramp caused the failures is inferred from correlation in the logs (error signature changing at 07:10 and error rate tracking the ramp), not from a confirmed fix - the one test of the hypothesis, reverting the flag, failed to restore service.

The investigator's later claim that toggling the flag off and back on reproduces the failure is not supported by anything in this record; no successful off-state was ever observed after 07:10, so no reproduction actually occurred.
Why the revert did not take effect was not established. It is assumed, not shown, that the flag-evaluation log lines after 07:16 accurately reflect the flag state the serving code saw.
Baseline behaviour is taken from the ten minutes before onset (07:00-07:09) plus the 360 minutes of metrics read, and is assumed representative of normal operation for this service and time of day.
Impact is assumed to be confined to the account page, because that is the only endpoint appearing in the logs read; no other endpoints or downstream consumers were checked.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 07:10 UTC on 28 September 2026, the account page of the online shop began failing for a large share of the shoppers who loaded it - roughly a third of those requests returned an error, against about one in a hundred beforehand. The page was still failing at the last minute of data we have, so the outage lasted at least eleven minutes and we do not know from this record when it ended; the same caveat applies to any statement about how many shoppers were affected. Other parts of the shop show no sign of being involved. Automated response picked the alert up about six minutes after the failures began, identified a newly switched-on account-page feature as the likely trigger, and switched that feature back off within a minute. Service did not recover, and the logs suggest the feature was still switched on afterwards, so the automated attempt was treated as unsuccessful and the incident was escalated to on-call engineers about ten minutes after the failures began. No other remedial action was taken. At hand-off the service was still failing and the fix was still unknown.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag was ramped from off to on between 07:09 and 07:11, which put traffic onto a code path containing a latent divide-by-zero (`ZeroDivisionError` at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47) on the io-shop account page; every account-page log line from 07:10 onward carries that exception, where the preceding ten minutes show only ordinary client disconnects, and the error rate tracked the ramp (1-1.5% while off, 6% in the mixed minute at 07:10, ~30%+ once fully on). This is the best-supported explanation but it is not confirmed: the one corrective action taken, reverting that flag at 07:16:19, did not clear the errors, and the flag-evaluation log lines at 07:17, 07:18 and 07:19 still report the flag as on for all 200 evaluations. Either the revert never reached the serving path or something else is holding the flag on, and that gap was never closed before the incident was handed off.
